subtitle: Arithmetic-type properties: numeric_limits<T> for every fundamental type, plus the rounding and subnormal enumerations. A real self-contained implementation (not a std re-export), portable from C++98.
legend_blurb: numeric_limits<T> with self-contained per-type specialisations for every fundamental arithmetic type (integers derived generically from the type; floats from compiler-predefined macros + builtins), plus float_round_style and float_denorm_style. Full coverage from C++98; lowest()/max_digits10 back-ported below std's C++11.

symbols.name: numeric_limits
symbols.notes: Self-contained, NOT a re-export. Per-type specialisations for bool, every character type, every signed/unsigned integer, and float/double/long double, plus cv-qualified passthroughs. Integer limits derive signedness, digits and min()/max() from the type itself via an internal generic base (so the implementation-defined signedness of char/wchar_t is handled automatically) with no dependency on <climits> values. Floating-point limits read the compiler-predefined __FLT_*__/__DBL_*__/__LDBL_*__ macros, falling back to <cfloat> on compilers that do not predefine them; infinity()/quiet_NaN()/signaling_NaN() use compiler builtins, degrading to a documented best-effort where unavailable. long long / char16_t / char32_t specialisations appear from C++11 and char8_t from C++20 (gated by the underlying type's existence, not by re_std). RE_STD AHEAD OF STD on the member axis: the C++11 observers lowest() and max_digits10 are back-ported to every tier including C++98. Verified member-for-member against std::numeric_limits for all ~19 fundamental types across C++98/11/14/17/20/23.

symbols.name: float_round_style
symbols.notes: Plain (non-scoped) enum naming the rounding mode reported by numeric_limits<T>::round_style: round_indeterminate(-1), round_toward_zero(0), round_to_nearest(1), round_toward_infinity(2), round_toward_neg_infinity(3). A plain enum (matching std), so it works unchanged on C++98.

symbols.name: float_denorm_style
symbols.notes: Plain enum naming subnormal support reported by numeric_limits<T>::has_denorm: denorm_indeterminate(-1), denorm_absent(0), denorm_present(1). std deprecated this enum (and has_denorm/has_denorm_loss) in C++23; re_std still provides it for portability and deliberately attaches no deprecation attribute so existing code keeps compiling warning-free.
